goal: Prevent a client that never finishes sending an HTTP request from permanently occupying a connection slot on the RPC/REST server, which can starve out legitimate clients once rpcmaxconnections is reached.
reviewability: Needs rebase, marked dirty, and conflicts with three other open PRs from the same reviewer touching the same files.

One open technical question about whether Send() needs an extra deadline restart, author replied with reasoning but hodlinator has not yet responded (hodlinator)

result.summary: Adds a second 'completion deadline' timer to the HTTP server, separate from the existing idle timer, that starts on the first byte of a request and is not reset by subsequent reads. A client that trickles bytes in slowly without ever completing a request is now disconnected once -rpcservertimeout elapses, freeing its connection slot. Includes new unit and functional tests exercising the trickling scenario and confirming normal slow RPCs are unaffected.
result.problem: The existing idle timeout resets on every byte received, so a client that keeps sending data without ever completing a request can hold a connection slot indefinitely. Since connection slots are capped (default 16 or -rpcmaxconnections), a handful of such clients can starve out legitimate RPC/REST callers; the author notes impact is low by default since RPC binds to localhost.

categories.name: rpc
categories.evidence: Directly modifies src/httpserver.cpp and src/httpserver.h, the HTTP server machinery underlying RPC/REST, and adds targeted unit and functional tests for it. Labeled RPC/REST/ZMQ.
categories.rationale: P2 because it closes a real resource-exhaustion path in the HTTP server: 'a client that keeps sending bytes without ever completing a request can hold the connection for ever,' reproduced concretely by the author with rpcmaxconnections=2 and trickled bytes. The rpc category rubric explicitly lists 'resource exhaustion through the HTTP server' as a priority, but the author's own admission that 'the impact is low because RPC port binds to localhost by default' and the lack of any external report of this being exploited keeps it from P1.

result.card: This PR adds a second, non-resettable deadline to the HTTP server so that a client which keeps sending bytes without ever completing an HTTP request can no longer hold a connection slot indefinitely, addressing a connection-slot exhaustion issue reproduced by the author with rpcmaxconnections=2. The author notes real-world impact is low since the RPC port binds to localhost by default, framing this as a robustness fix rather than a remote security issue. hodlinator gave a Concept ACK and raised several review comments, most resolved in a 2026-09-14 rebase; one remark about a possibly-missing deadline restart in Send() got an author reply that has not yet been confirmed. The PR is marked Needs rebase and conflicts with three other open PRs from hodlinator touching the same httpserver files (#36159, #36160, #36124), so review timing should account for that overlap. No stated external dependency blocks the PR itself.
